correctness.rationale: For any n>=1 and any unrestricted relation R on the labelled n-chain, each row R[j] fails U_a->U_b exactly when nonempty and its minimum is in [a,b), because chain upset inclusion depends only on that minimum. The greatest violating j determines output U_{1+max ell_t}; adjacent-upset arguments recover each ell_t individually. Nonnegative ell_t are distinct as no row has two minima. Conversely singleton rows at ell_t realize every partial injection, so the operation census is sum_k binom(n,k)^2 k!. Every representing R must contain each edge (ell_t,t), hence the canonical singleton-row relation is the unique inclusion-minimum. At forced rows j=ell_t all choices are the w_t=2^(n-1-t) subsets with minimum t; optional rows are either empty or have minimum t with later last occurrence ell_t>j. Independence proves the stated exact product for all realization-fiber sizes. Independent direct semantic enumeration of relations for n<=3 verified counts 2,7,34 and fiber mechanism; inspected exhaustive package checker also implements n=4 but its previous pass was not substituted for proof.
